candidates.current_role: Grayson County Justice of the Peace, Precinct 2, appointed January 3, 2025
candidates.background: Dennis Michael was appointed Justice of the Peace for Precinct 2 on January 3, 2025. A lifelong Grayson County resident, he served 27 years with the Sherman Police Department and 24 years as an investigator for the Grayson County Criminal District Attorney's Office. He holds an associate degree from Grayson College and a criminal justice degree from Southeastern Oklahoma State University, and is a former Pottsboro city councilman.

notes.text: His county biography lists past service as a Republican Party of Grayson County precinct chair and as board president of CASA of Grayson County.

candidates.current_role: Judge, 246th Family District Court, Harris County
candidates.background: Angela Graves-Harrington presides over the 246th District Court, a Harris County family court. Her court biography says she is the first woman elected to that bench and is board certified in family law. She helped develop the Child Welfare Clinic at Thurgood Marshall School of Law, where she is an adjunct professor. Branch reports she has been on the bench since 2019, holds a J.D. from Thurgood Marshall School of Law and a bachelor's degree from Jackson State University, and previously practiced family law.

record.text: Her court biography says the Supreme Court of Texas Children's Commission chose her court as one of six trauma-informed project courts in Texas, and that she was appointed to the Children's Commission in 2020.

candidates.current_role: Harris County Justice of the Peace, Precinct 1, Place 2, elected November 2022
candidates.background: Steve Duble was elected Justice of the Peace for Precinct 1, Place 2 in November 2022, after more than 30 years practicing law in Harris County. His court biography says he graduated from Strake Jesuit, Texas Christian University (1986) and the University of Houston Law Center (1989), and calls him the first openly gay JP in Harris County history.

notes.text: In April 2026 the State Commission on Judicial Conduct publicly admonished him and ordered two hours of extra education. It found he failed to timely hear property exemption claims in about ten cases and ended two receiverships without notice or a hearing.

sources.title: Steve Duble, Justice of the Peace Precinct 1, Place 2
